result.summary:
READ-ONLY audit of /n/home04/yulili/bgfm/paper (main.tex + sections/{01_intro,02_method,03_theory,04_experiments,05_conclusion,A1_proofs,A2_details}.tex + the six live figure/table files; fig1_method.tex, fig2_boltzmann.tex, fig3_ablation.tex and tabA1_cells.tex are NOT input by main.tex and were checked but need no edit). No files were modified.

N1 DENSITY NOTATION. 131 occurrences of p_\theta across the live sources. Every one that denotes the supervised/evaluated object is the clamped positional-flow density and must become q_\theta. Only three sites genuinely mean the joint generator's conditional density and must keep p: sections/A1_proofs.tex:91 (Assumption A2's contrast clause), sections/02_method.tex:88 (disclosure iii), sections/A2_details.tex:1394 (limitation vi-d). The definition must be planted once, in Sec. 3 immediately after eq:ffjord, and mirrored in Assumption A2. Figure 1 needs both its caption (figures/fig1_objective_float.tex:39-40) and its in-figure TikZ text (figures/fig1_objective.tex:219-220) rewritten to the required wording, plus the two added statements (this is the object supervised and evaluated; it need not equal the joint generator's conditional density).

N2 ESTIMATOR PROSE. The eps = 1/(2n) smoothing-scale reading is load-bearing in 5 of the 7 .tex sources and must come out everywhere per FINDING 1. Hard deletions: eq:epsgrid itself (02_method.tex:77-80) and all six \eqref{eq:epsgrid} call sites; the "smoothed marginal log p_{1-eps}" sentence (02_method.tex:81-86); Appendix A.2 Step 3 (A1_proofs.tex:249-276); rem:epscert (A1_proofs.tex:484-492); the tab:epsgrid caption and the whole framing of app:estimator (A2_details.tex:304-472); limitation (vi-a) (A2_details.tex:1356-1366). Under the corrected reading the resolution rows say something less comfortable, and that must be written: the gap is largest where the estimator is least accurate (+0.382 at n=4) and shrinks as it becomes more accurate (+0.177 at n=12), the headline is computed at n=12, and the design cannot separate a genuine scale dependence from Euler bias. Naming must be unified to "explicit Euler in the state with midpoint-rule quadrature for the divergence integral": tabA2_constants.tex:36 says "reverse-time Euler", A1_proofs.tex:249 says "first-order midpoint scheme", and each is half right. The "principled repair" paragraph (A2_details.tex:463-472) is now describing a repair of a defect that does not exist and must be replaced by the real open item (validate the estimator; the Euler state error, not the quadrature, dominates). NO RETRAINING is triggered and none should be proposed.

Separately, FINDING 2 requires a main-text disclosure that the L_value gradient is a truncated-adjoint surrogate; it currently lives only in A2_details.tex:62-75 and limitation (viii). Recommended insertion point: 02_method.tex disclosure (iv).

N3 OVERCLAIM SWEEP. The paper is in good shape here — the forbidden phrases are largely absent. "learns a Boltzmann distribution": no occurrence, but A2_details.tex:133 ("the object trained is the Boltzmann distribution at that kT") is the nearest thing and should be NARROWed. "thermodynamically correct": no occurrence. "basin occupancy": six occurrences (03_theory.tex:68, 05_conclusion.tex:66, 01_intro.tex:72, A1_proofs.tex:641-642/716, A2_details.tex:1334), all identifiability statements or explicit non-claims — KEEP. "improves global molecular physicality": no occurrence. "the generator's exact conditional density": no occurrence; the three "generator's own conditional density" sites are correctly conditional ("only if") — KEEP. "force supervision fails": no occurrence; the scoped statement at 04_experiments.tex:218-227 carries all four qualifiers — KEEP; but the abstract (01_intro.tex:21-22) and the intro finding (01_intro.tex:84-85) drop qualifiers and should be NARROWed. "generation quality is preserved": no occurrence, but the Sec. 5.5 title asserts it — see N4. "numerically robust": only as an explicit disclaimer (04_experiments.tex:315) — KEEP. "exact likelihood training": only as an explicit disclaimer (A2_details.tex:74) — KEEP, and promote to main text. Four hits for "Boltzmann generator" in the rendered PDF are all bibliography titles of cited prior work, not descriptions of our model.

N4 GENERATION QUALITY. Evidence is one value seed against two control seeds at n=100 samples, binomial SE ~5 points against differences of a few points, and the control's own seeds are 41.0 and 30.0. Section 5.5's title "What is preserved, and what remains unresolved?" asserts preservation and must be retitled to a question; the body's "at or above our flow-matching control's" is a comparative claim the design cannot support; and 05_conclusion.tex:46 ("reported only to show it is not degraded") asserts a demonstration. The appendix (A2_details.tex:1133-1145) is already correctly hedged and is the model the main text should follow.

N5 RELATED WORK GAP. VERIFIED. "Energy-Based Flow Matching for Generating 3D Molecular Structure", Wenyin Zhou, Christopher Iliffe Sprague, Vsevolod Viliuga, Matteo Tadiello, Arne Elofsson, Hossein Azizpour; ICML 2025; arXiv:2508.18949. I confirmed from the arXiv PDF text that the method IS named IDFlow (the ICML virtual page's claim to the contrary is wrong) and that its energy is the reconstruction error ||x - x_hat||, driving an idempotent predictor-refiner. No idflow key exists in refs.bib (41 entries). Proposed entry and contrast sentence given below; placement in the "Energy-targeted samplers" paragraph (01_intro.tex:159-174). Not needed as an experimental baseline.

PRIORITY ORDER: (1) plant the q_\theta definition and fix Figure 1, since every other N1 edit depends on it; (2) excise eq:epsgrid and rewrite app:estimator, since limitation (vi) and Sec. 5.5 both inherit from it; (3) the four N3/N4 narrowings; (4) the IDFlow citation.

sites.classification: N2 DELETE + REWRITE (the root of the whole eps thread)
sites.context: Lines 75-86. Displays $\epsilon = 1/(2n)$ as eq:epsgrid and concludes "what \eqref{eq:lvalue} and every density here refer to is the \emph{smoothed} marginal $\log p_{1-\epsilon}$, not $\log p_1$: refining the grid estimates a different, less smoothed quantity rather than the same one more accurately, and no convergence in $n$ is expected or observed." Training uses $n = 4$ and every reported evaluation $n = 12$, the more accurate of the two; we disclose the mismatch and measure its effect (\Cref{sec:openquestions},~\Cref{app:estimator})."

sites.classification: N2 REWRITE (this is the honest-consequence paragraph)
sites.context: Lines 297-308: "The effect size is \emph{resolution-conditional}: the estimator's smoothing scale is tied to its step count by \eqref{eq:epsgrid} ... puts the gap at $+0.382$ at $\epsilon = 0.125$, where the objective trains, and $+0.177$ at $\epsilon = 0.042$ ... this design cannot separate a genuine scale-dependence from a resolution-matching artefact ... its size is a property of the smoothing scale as well as of the model."
sites.replacement: "The effect size depends on the estimator's step count. A strictly paired re-scoring of existing checkpoints, with identical parents and displacements at each resolution, puts the gap at $+0.382$ at $n = 4$, where the objective trains, and $+0.177$ at $n = 12$, where every number here is computed. Both rows estimate the same quantity, so the gap is largest where the estimator is least accurate and shrinks as it becomes more accurate --- an ordering consistent with part of the coarse-resolution effect being solver artefact. The headline is computed at $n = 12$. This design cannot separate a genuine scale dependence of the learned density from Euler bias, because the training step count and the coarsest evaluation step count coincide by construction. A finer $n = 48$ cell rests on one value-arm evaluation, is not powered, and we report no value for it."

sites.item: N2: the "no plateau" paragraph
sites.classification: N2 REWRITE (the measurement stands; its interpretation inverts)
sites.context: Lines 335-348. "The flow-matching marginal is singular as $t \to 1$ ... so $\log p_{1-\epsilon}$ has no finite $\epsilon \to 0$ limit on a fixed molecule. The behaviour is exactly that. Re-scoring the same ten held-out molecules ... gives mean $\log p_\theta$ of $-65.5$, $-114.3$, $-199.9$ ... a step-count sweep of this estimator cannot be read as a convergence check on one quantity." Under FINDING 1 it IS a convergence check on one quantity, and it fails.
sites.replacement: Retitle "No plateau is reached, and the measurement that shows it". Body: "All three step counts estimate the same $\log q_\theta$, so a step-count sweep \emph{is} a convergence check --- and it does not pass. Re-scoring the same ten held-out molecules at the three step counts of \Cref{tab:epsgrid} gives mean $\log q_\theta$ of $-65.5$ ($n = 4$), $-114.3$ ($n = 12$) and $-199.9$ ($n = 48$): each refinement removes a further $49$ and then $86$ nats, with no sign of a plateau. On an analytic linear problem the same integrator converges cleanly to the exact endpoint value, so the drift here is a property of the learned field's endpoint stiffness and of the $O(\Delta t)$ Euler state error at these step counts, not of the scheme's target. We report this as a disclosure and not as a convergence study --- ten molecules is a small sample --- and no statement of the form \emph{$\log q_\theta$ is converged at $n$ steps} is available for this implementation."

sites.item: N2: "Training and evaluation run at different smoothing scales"
sites.context: Lines 349-355. "Training and evaluation therefore constrain and measure log-densities at different smoothing scales. This is a defect of the implementation rather than of the objective."
sites.replacement: Retitle "Training and evaluation run at different accuracies". "The value term is evaluated at $n = 4$ because a continuous-flow objective inside the training loop is otherwise unaffordable, while every reported evaluation runs at $n = 12$. Both target the same $\log q_\theta$; the training term therefore constrains a more coarsely discretised estimate of the same quantity the metric measures more accurately. We cannot say whether that attenuates the reported effect, inflates it, or is immaterial (\Cref{app:limitations} item (vi))."

The headline is computed at $n = 12$, the more accurate of the two." VERIFIED — the record exists and the brief's characterisation is accurate. Title: "Energy-Based Flow Matching for Generating 3D Molecular Structure". Authors, in order: Wenyin Zhou, Christopher Iliffe Sprague, Vsevolod Viliuga, Matteo Tadiello, Arne Elofsson, Hossein Azizpour. arXiv:2508.18949, submitted 26 August 2025; the arXiv comments field records acceptance to ICML 2025, and an ICML 2025 poster page (icml.cc/virtual/2025/poster/44407) and an OpenReview forum (id=hcJWWC82KW) both exist for it.

One correction worth recording, because the sources disagree. The ICML virtual page's rendering states the method is NOT named IDFlow. That is wrong. I pulled the arXiv PDF and grepped its text directly: "IDFlow" appears throughout — Figure 1's caption reads "Training paradigm of standard flow matching and IDFlow", and the introduction reads "our trained idempotent function (IDFlow) simultaneously serves as both a neural sampler and a refiner". The brief's description of the core is also confirmed from the same text: "we take the reconstruction error ||x - x_hat|| as the [energy]", with low energy assigned to good predictions, and an idempotent objective that lets the map iteratively refine its own sample. So the proposed contrast sentence is factually correct as written and needs no softening.

The contrast is genuine and worth stating: their energy is internal to the model (a reconstruction residual, learned), ours is external and physical (values from a universal neural potential trained on DFT); their setting is conditional protein docking and backbone generation with the target identity supplied, ours is bond-free de novo molecular generation where composition is generated; and their energy shapes the sampling trajectory, whereas ours supervises and diagnoses a tractable density. Not needed as an experimental baseline.

Caveat for the citation-check pass: the venue/date pairing (ICML 2025, but arXiv submission dated August 2025, after the conference) is the normal post-acceptance-posting pattern and is consistent across the arXiv abstract page, the ICML virtual page and the survey that cites it; no discrepancy needs resolving, but the entry carries a note field recording it.

sites.problem: The edge condition is too weak. Taken literally $S$ may be the whole space, in which case every pair of nonzero measures is joined. More importantly the condition does not force two almost-sure constancy statements to agree anywhere: two mutually singular measures can each charge a common set while their exceptional sets cover each other's mass, so no single point need carry both identities. The definition is also inconsistent with its own proof, which uses $S = U_j \cap U_{j'}$ (A1_proofs.tex:604) rather than the stated condition.
sites.replacement:
\begin{definition}[Overlap graph]
\label{def:overlap}
Fix a composition $c$ with groups $j = 1,\dots,J$ and reference measures $\rho_j$ with supports
$U_j$, all dominated by a common $\sigma$-finite measure $\mu$, and write
$f_j = \mathrm{d}\rho_j/\mathrm{d}\mu$. The \emph{overlap graph} $\mathcal{G}_c$ has vertices
$\{1,\dots,J\}$ and an edge $\{j,j'\}$ if and only if
\begin{equation}
  \int \min\bigl(f_j, f_{j'}\bigr)\,\mathrm{d}\mu \;>\; 0 ,
  \label{eq:overlap}
\end{equation}
equivalently if and only if $\rho_j$ and $\rho_{j'}$ are \emph{not mutually singular}. The
criterion does not depend on the choice of $\mu$. An edge supplies the measure
$\mathrm{d}\nu = \min(f_j,f_{j'})\,\mathrm{d}\mu$, which is nonzero and absolutely continuous
with respect to both $\rho_j$ and $\rho_{j'}$; that is what forces the two constancy statements
to agree, and it is what a set merely charged by both measures does not supply. Overlap here is a
property of the measures and not of the topological supports: $U_j \cap U_{j'} \neq \emptyset$ is
necessary for an edge but far from sufficient.
\end{definition}

\begin{proposition}[Objective conflict]
\label{prop:conflict}
The population minimiser of $\Ls_{\mathrm{FM}}$ has implied score
$\nabla \log p^{\mathrm{data}}_t$, whereas $\Ls_{\mathrm{force}}$ drives
$s_\theta \to \nabla \log \pi$. If $p_{\mathrm{data}} \neq \pi$ these targets differ

\begin{theorem}[Gauge-identifiability]
\label{thm:gauge}
Assume (B1) for each $c$ the coordinate domain is connected and $E(c,\cdot)$ is
$C^1$ (\Cref{ass:A1}); (B2) the estimator accesses only
$\{\nabla_{\vx} E(c,\vx)\}$, not absolute energies (\Cref{ass:B}); (B3)
compositions are compared through the joint density. Then force information
identifies the conditional $\pi(\cdot \mid c)$ exactly for every $c$, but the joint
$\pi(c,\vx)$ only up to $E \mapsto E + g(c)$, which leaves every force and every
conditional invariant while reweighting the joint by $e^{-g(c)/kT}$. The
unidentifiable degrees of freedom are exactly the per-composition free energies
$\{A(c)\}$.
\end{theorem}

At 1e-4, M=8 energy: surrogate ΔL = −1.55 against full ΔL = −15.9, i.e. the surrogate captures about a tenth of the available decrease at that step on that batch.

- It does not break for cost reasons at the sizes that matter. One-variant-per-process cost table (`p1_surrgrad_cost-39959842.out`, 32 cells): peak RSS differs by <1% between full and surrogate at every synthetic setting (e.g. 72 atoms, n_ode=12, exact divergence: 46 392 MB surrogate vs 46 443 MB full); backward-pass time is 5–26% slower for full (9.75 s vs 7.72 s at that cell). After I freed each graph after reading its value, the same cell ran to completion (job 39960005, all M=1/2/4/8 cells for both checkpoints). Honest boundary: with the naive harness the break is at ~780 atoms / n_ode=4 on 140 GB; with one graph at a time it is above that, and I did not find its ceiling.

CONSEQUENCE FOR THE MANUSCRIPT (as you already intended): the method must be described as optimising a truncated-adjoint surrogate of the clamped positional-flow log-density, not the likelihood itself. The measurement supports the weaker, defensible claim — the surrogate is a consistently positively-correlated descent direction (cos ≈ 0.58 for the training loss and ≈ 0.76 for the ordering objective at the training-matched setting, never negative in 152 pairs) — and does not support calling it likelihood-gradient descent. The attenuation is not uniform across the network (43/415 tensors anti-aligned, late layers worst), so the surrogate also changes which parameters move, not just how far.
